examples.title: A TSA response against the request that was sent and the data
A bare token against the digest it stamps

description: The one-call verdict on an RFC 3161 time-stamp: exactly one of `token` (a TimeStampToken, .tst) or `response` (the whole TimeStampResp, .tsr — a declined response is PKI_REASON_TSP_NOT_GRANTED), judged against what YOU say was stamped — `request` (the .tsq you sent: imprint, nonce and policy are all checked, the only way to catch a replay), `data` (hashed with the token's own algorithm) or `digestHex`; at least one is required, because a token verified without what it stamps proves nothing (VALIDATION_ERROR otherwise). The TSA's signature is verified, its certificate must chain to one of YOUR `trustAnchors` (through `candidates` and the certificates the token carries) at `at` with a critical timeStamping EKU (allowNonCriticalTimeStampingEku:true for deployed TSAs that are not), and revocation is judged from the CRL / OCSP bytes YOU supply (`requireRevocation:true` demands evidence). A negative verdict is valid:false + reasons[] (PKI_REASON_* codes) — never isError. genTime / earliest / latest (accuracy applied) are established only when valid. Pin `at` for a reproducible, cacheable verdict. Token-frugal: verbosity:'summary'.

allowNonCriticalTimeStampingEku.description: Accept a TSA whose extKeyUsage names timeStamping but is not critical (RFC 3161 §2.3 requires it critical; some deployed TSAs are not).

allowSha1.description: Accept or produce SHA-1 signatures (legacy material you already trust). Default false: refused with PKI_CRYPTO_ALGORITHM_REFUSED on read, VALIDATION_ERROR on write.

at.description: The instant the verdict is evaluated at. An ISO 8601 date-time (UTC unless zoned; e.g. 2027-01-01T00:00:00Z), epoch milliseconds as digits, or 'now'. Omitted: PKINATIVE_MCP_AT when the operator pinned it, else the wall clock (a clock-dependent result is never cached).

candidates.description: Untrusted certificates the TSA's path may use (every PEM block of every item is taken). Optional; the certificates the token carries are also candidates.

items.description: Untrusted intermediate certificates the path may use: exactly one of pem / derBase64 / path.

derBase64.description: DER bytes as base64, exactly once (not PEM text).

path.description: Relative path of a PEM / DER file inside the PKINATIVE_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR sandbox (never cached).

crls.description: CRLs (DER or X509 CRL PEM) for offline revocation (every PEM block of every item is taken). Optional; this server never fetches a CRL — pass the bytes you obtained.

items.description: CRLs (DER or X509 CRL PEM) for offline revocation: exactly one of pem / derBase64 / path.

derBase64.description: DER bytes as base64, exactly once (not PEM text).

path.description: Relative path of a PEM / DER file inside the PKINATIVE_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR sandbox (never cached).

data.description: The data that was stamped (hashed with the token's own imprint algorithm): exactly one of text / base64 / path.

base64.description: The data that was stamped (hashed with the token's own imprint algorithm) as base64 bytes (≤ 128 MiB decoded). Exclusive with text / path.

path.description: Relative path of a file inside the sandbox (any extension, ≤ 1 GiB). Exclusive with text / base64.

text.description: The data that was stamped (hashed with the token's own imprint algorithm) as UTF-8 text. Exclusive with base64 / path.

digestHex.description: The digest that was stamped, when you hold that rather than the data. Exclusive with data. Hexadecimal (an 0x prefix, colons and spaces are tolerated).

encodingRules.description: 'der' (strict X.690 DER, default) or 'ber' (indefinite / non-minimal lengths and constructed strings, as legacy CMS producers write).

fields.description: Dot-paths to keep after verbosity (arrays map over elements); unmatched paths land in _meta.unmatchedFields.

limits.description: Raise pkinative's 22 named security bounds for this call (trusted input only; absent keys keep the engine defaults). A value above an operator ceiling (PKINATIVE_MCP_MAX_INPUT_BYTES, PKINATIVE_MCP_MAX_KDF_ITERATIONS, PKINATIVE_MCP_MAX_PATHS_EXPLORED) is LIMIT_CEILING_EXCEEDED; describe_engine lists the defaults and the ceilings.

maxAttributes.description: The attributes of one attribute set. Default 256.

maxBerSegments.description: The segments joined from one BER constructed string. Default 10000.

maxChainLength.description: The certificates one certification path may hold. Default 10.

maxCmsCertificatesAndCrls.description: The certificates and revocation entries one SignedData carries. Default 1024.

maxDepth.description: The nesting depth of constructed values. Default 64.

maxExtensions.description: The extensions of one certificate or request. Default 256.

maxGeneralNames.description: The GeneralName entries of one field. Default 10000.

maxInputBytes.description: The size of one DER input, or the length of one PEM text. Default 67108864.

maxIntegerBytes.description: The content length of one INTEGER converted to a bigint. Default 8192.

maxKdfIterations.description: The PBKDF2 iteration count honoured in one derivation. Default 10000000.

maxNameAttributes.description: The attributes of one distinguished name. Default 1024.

maxNodes.description: The number of values decoded from one input. Default 200000.

maxOcspSingleResponses.description: The SingleResponse entries of one OCSP response. Default 256.

maxOidBytes.description: The content length of one OBJECT IDENTIFIER. Default 256.

maxPathsExplored.description: The candidate paths explored while building one (the RFC 5280 §6 work bound). Default 1000.

maxPemBlocks.description: The blocks read from one PEM text. Default 10000.

maxPkcs12Bags.description: The SafeBags read from one PKCS#12, across every SafeContents. Default 4096.

maxPkcs12KdfIterations.description: The PBKDF2 iterations one PKCS#12 costs in total. Default 10000000.

maxPolicies.description: The policies or policy mappings of one extension. Default 1024.

maxPolicyNodes.description: The live nodes of the RFC 5280 valid_policy_tree. Default 4096.

maxRevokedCertificates.description: The entries walked in one CRL revokedCertificates list. Default 1000000.

maxSignerInfos.description: The signers of one SignedData. Default 64.

ocspResponses.description: OCSP responses (DER) for offline revocation (every PEM block of every item is taken). Optional; this server never queries a responder — pass the bytes you obtained.

items.description: OCSP responses (DER) for offline revocation: exactly one of pem / derBase64 / path.

derBase64.description: DER bytes as base64, exactly once (not PEM text).

path.description: Relative path of a PEM / DER file inside the PKINATIVE_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR sandbox (never cached).

pemMode.description: 'strict' (RFC 7468 exactly, default) or 'lax' (tolerates whitespace, line length and RFC 1421 headers).

request.description: The TimeStampReq you sent (.tsq): exactly one of pem / derBase64 / path. The strongest statement of what was stamped: imprint, nonce and policy are all checked; the only way to catch a replayed response.

derBase64.description: DER bytes as base64, exactly once (not PEM text).

path.description: Relative path of a PEM / DER file inside the PKINATIVE_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR sandbox (never cached).

requireRevocation.description: Require fresh revocation evidence for the end-entity certificate (PKI_REASON_REVOCATION_UNKNOWN otherwise — the engine demands it for the leaf; an intermediate is judged from the evidence you pass); default false = revocation is checked when evidence is given.

response.description: The whole TimeStampResp the TSA returned (.tsr): exactly one of pem / derBase64 / path. Exclusive with token. A response that granted nothing is PKI_REASON_TSP_NOT_GRANTED.

derBase64.description: DER bytes as base64, exactly once (not PEM text).

path.description: Relative path of a PEM / DER file inside the PKINATIVE_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR sandbox (never cached).

strict.description: Escalate the first engine warning to a PKI_STRICT_DIAGNOSTIC error instead of listing it in diagnostics[].

token.description: The TimeStampToken (a ContentInfo over a TSTInfo; .tst): exactly one of pem / derBase64 / path. Exclusive with response.

derBase64.description: DER bytes as base64, exactly once (not PEM text).

path.description: Relative path of a PEM / DER file inside the PKINATIVE_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR sandbox (never cached).

trustAnchors.description: Trust anchors (root certificates you trust) (every PEM block of every item is taken). At least one is required: a verdict is relative to the anchors you name.

items.description: Trust anchors (root certificates you trust): exactly one of pem / derBase64 / path.

derBase64.description: DER bytes as base64, exactly once (not PEM text).

path.description: Relative path of a PEM / DER file inside the PKINATIVE_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR sandbox (never cached).

name: verify_timestamp

outputSchema.description: Time-stamp verdict. Every property is optional because the result can be projected: verbosity:'summary' returns only the scalar summary fields, fields:[...] keeps a dot-path subset. Defaults return the full shape.

chain.description: The chain judged by verify_certificate_chain, or null when there was no certificate to judge.

reasons.description: Why the verdict is negative (empty when valid): the engine PKI_REASON_* codes, each with the standard it cites and the path of the offending element. A reason is returned, never thrown.

errorCode.description: The PKI_* error the parser would have thrown (PKI_REASON_INPUT_MALFORMED).

diagnostics.description: Non-fatal concerns the engine raised (PKI_DIAG_*, de-duplicated, at most 200; explain_code explains one).

diagnosticsTruncated.description: true when distinct diagnostics beyond the 200 listed were dropped.

evaluatedAt.description: The ISO instant the TSA chain was judged at — re-pass it as `at` to reproduce the verdict.

genTime.description: The time the TSA asserts (ISO 8601) — established only when valid.

latest.description: genTime plus the declared accuracy — the instant an LTV check compares against.

reasons.description: Why the verdict is negative (empty when valid): the engine PKI_REASON_* codes, each with the standard it cites and the path of the offending element. A reason is returned, never thrown.

errorCode.description: The PKI_* error the parser would have thrown (PKI_REASON_INPUT_MALFORMED).

tsa.description: The TSA certificate whose key verified the token, or null.

valid.description: Whether the token is evidence that the expected hash existed at genTime. false is a negative verdict (reasons[]), never an error.
